Open Handy Horology Helper. Swipe the welcome slides. With HHH you can identify a piece, keep a museum, and hunt on eBay — so you can fill in the details in the moment, then keep what you own.
On the last welcome slide, tap Get Started. You land on How do you want to start?
If you'd like a tour first, tap Explore with sample collection — Ludwig's demo gallery — so you can tap around before you add a real piece.
Or tap Start with my own piece to add your first watch from the camera or by typing, so the museum starts with something that is yours.
If you picked sample collection, wait while Ludwig's demo watches load, then tap Get Started on the confirmation screen.
When sample data is active, notice the banner reminding you these are demo pieces — so you do not mix them with yours.
Tap Clear samples on the Home banner when you are ready for your own museum, so the counts and values are yours.
You land on Home — the Command Center. The status line shows piece count and wish-list size, a quick read before you open a tab.
Tap Hunt on the quick command row for eBay grails — so HHH can watch a piece you want. Fix clock opens Clock Repair Help. Add Watch opens My Museum. Tools opens the toolkit.
Getting started path cards jump straight to Hunt on eBay, troubleshoot a clock, start your museum, or identify a piece — pick the job you came to do.
The bottom tab bar has five tabs: Home, My Museum, Tools, Collectors, and Settings. That's how you move between the main parts of the app.
Tap the My Museum tab — second icon from the left — to open your collection, so every piece you own or want sits in one place.
Tap Owned at the top to see your collection. Wish holds grail targets; For Sale lists pieces you are selling. Split that way so a want does not look like you already own it.
The hero card shows total estimated value, gain or loss, and a sparkline of collection value over time — so you can see if the museum is up or down without a spreadsheet.
Tap the search field and type a brand or model. The list filters as you type, so you can find one piece without scrolling the whole museum.
Tap any row to open Piece Detail — photos, provenance, service history, and estimated value — so the facts sit with the piece.
On Piece Detail, swipe the photo gallery. Brand, model, reference, and estimated value sit below the photos.
Tap Provenance to record where you bought the piece, serial numbers, and collector notes — so a later buyer or an insurer is not starting from a blank page.
Repairs and Service logs cleanings, repairs, and costs — each entry updates your cost basis, so gain and loss stay honest.
Tap the Wish segment to see grail targets linked to hunt rules — pieces HHH can watch on eBay for you.
Tap For Sale to list pieces you are actively selling with asking price and notes, so asking and owned stay separate.
On My Pieces, tap More for Timeline, Finances, Insurance Report, Service Tracker, and eBay match alerts — the money and hunt tools in one menu.
On My Pieces, tap the gold Add button on the action bar — center of the bottom bar — when you want a piece on the list tonight.
Tap Enter details manually if you want to type the piece in yourself — not Identify — useful when you already know the name.
Fill Maker or brand, model, reference, serial, purchase price, and notes so the museum card is complete enough to find later.
Tap Save to Museum. The piece is in your Owned collection right away.

With Handy Horology Helper you can identify a piece from a photo — year, metal, worth, and the rest of the details — so you can buy, pass, or bid while the piece is still in front of you. Tap Identify on My Museum — or open Tools and tap Identify.
Here's how. Take one clear dial photo. One is enough. Extra shots are optional.
Or tap Choose Photo for a picture you already have — a shop, a show, an estate — so you do not have to reshoot if the piece is gone.
If it asks for a movement or caseback photo, skip it unless you have it. A dial shot is enough to start.
What do you know is optional. Fill in only what you already have — a name on the dial helps; blanks are fine.
Scroll to Wristwatch, Pocket Watch, or Clock if the type is wrong, so the answer matches what you are holding.
When you have a photo, tap Identify. You can leave the other fields blank. The details come up next.
On the results, tap the top match. Other possibilities is there if you want to compare.
If the top match looks right, keep it. If not, pick another from the list below.
You might want a closer shot of bezel text, a logo, or a serial. Tap Add detail photos, then Identify again — extra facts when the first pass was thin.
Tap What I know to correct brand or model, then tap Identify again, so a name you already read on the dial is in the answer.
Tap Save to Museum. The piece lands in Owned with the photo, name, and estimated value filled in, so you do not retype it later.
If you'd like parts after a clock ID, open Tools and tap Find Clock Parts — so a movement you just identified can point at the parts that fit.
If you'd like Identify at a show with no signal, turn on a pack here before you go — wrist, pocket, or clock — so you still have a pocket reference when the room has no Wi-Fi.
Here's Clock Repair Help. Tap the symptom that matches — won't chime, pendulum stops, or another from the list — so you get steps for that problem, not a generic lecture.
Find Clock Parts is also on Tools. Movement to Parts sits next to it — same job from a movement photo if you already have one.
Pick the symptom that matches: Won't chime, Pendulum stops, Hands slip, or another option from the list.
Review the plain-language repair steps HHH suggests for your symptom. Follow safety notes before opening the case.
Scroll to Suggested parts. SKUs and product names appear when the catalog is connected, so you can see what to order without guessing a number.
A product row or Shop opens the item in your browser so you can finish the order there.
Complete checkout on the parts site — HHH does not process payments for parts.
With HHH you can hunt a grail on eBay. Tap Hunt on Home — or open My Pieces and switch to Wish — so HHH can watch for that piece without you refreshing all day.
Tap the plus button on Wish list. Enter brand, model, and a target price you are willing to pay, so the hunt has a ceiling.
Tap a wish-list row to open the hunt for that grail. Hunt rules and last-check time appear at the top, so you can see what it is watching.
Edit keywords and max price under Hunt rules. Tap Save hunt rules when done.
Tap Check now to search eBay immediately. Matches appear with listing title, price, and link — so you can look while the listing is still up.
Any match opens the eBay listing in your browser.
When a new match arrives, HHH sends a notification. Tap it to jump straight to that grail, so you do not miss it.
From Tools, open eBay Listings to search sold and active listings by brand and model — comps before you commit.
Enter brand and model, then review active and sold comps before you commit to a purchase.
On My Pieces, tap More, then Finances — or Gains and Losses — for portfolio-level profit and loss, so you can see if the museum is earning or costing.
The dashboard shows total cost basis, estimated value, and net gain or loss across all owned pieces.
On any Piece Detail screen, tap Edit and enter Purchase price. HHH recalculates gain or loss against estimated value.
Under Repairs and Service, Add entry takes date, vendor, and cost — service spend adds to your cost basis, so a big service does not hide in a notebook.
From More, Insurance Report builds a PDF-ready summary of pieces, values, and photos for your insurer — so you are not rebuilding the museum by hand.
From Finances or the More menu, open Budget Tracker, so a month of buys has a cap you can see.
Set a monthly or annual acquisition budget and track spend against it as you add pieces.
From Tools, open Web Companion and tap Start. Your phone shows a local address and a large four-digit pairing code — the bigger screen when you are reviewing the museum.
On a PC on the same Wi-Fi, open that address in a browser, then type the four-digit code shown on the phone.
On the PC dashboard, browse pieces, add watches, and manage hunts — changes sync back to the phone, so you are not keeping two lists.
Open Settings, then File backup — or open File backup from Tools — to manage your portable backup, so a new phone can pick up the museum.
Tap Save a Copy. Choose Drive, Files, email, or another share destination for the backup file.
On another phone, tap Bring a Copy Back and pick your backup file. Confirm before it adds or replaces museum data — so a bad restore does not wipe you by surprise.
Optional: tap Device Sync to move pieces between your own phones or tablets on the same Wi-Fi. Cloud sync stays optional — your museum lives on the device first.
Tap the Settings tab — gear icon at bottom right.
Tap Theme and switch Light or Dark. The app updates immediately.
Tap Language. Pick the language you read, then confirm.

On Security and App Lock, turn the lock on if you want the app to make you enter your PIN or show your face every time you open it — even though the phone is already unlocked. Canceling or failing leaves HHH locked.
The museum lives on the phone. That line in Settings is just saying the same thing.
When a hunt match lands, HHH can send a notification — tap it to jump straight to that grail. Allow notifications when the phone asks, so hunt alerts and service reminders can reach you.
HHH includes a 15-day Pro trial with full access — no credit card — so you can try the toolkit before you pay. Cancel anytime.
After the trial, tap Upgrade in Settings. Choose $9.99 per month or $74.99 per year.
Manage cancels or changes your subscription through Google Play or the App Store.
Tap the Tools tab — center icon — to open the toolkit.
Tap What's It Worth when you want a price read on a piece you already know — Pro.
Tap Compare. Pick two pieces from your museum to see side-by-side specs, value, and photos — useful when you cannot remember which one you meant.
Tap Condition Assessment. Answer checklist questions about case, dial, and movement so you and a buyer are using the same words.
Tap Collection Value to see how your portfolio estimated value changed over time.
Trade Analyzer models a trade — your piece plus cash versus theirs — Pro — so you can see the trade before you say yes. Find it further down the Tools list.
Tap Ask the Expert when you want a horology question answered in plain language — Pro.
Tap Photo Coach for guided shots — dial, caseback, movement — Pro — so the next Identify or listing photo is usable.
Tap Digital ID Card to generate a proof-of-ownership card with photos and key details — Pro — handy when you need to show the piece without handing it over.
Scan Barcode points the camera at a UPC or QR on packaging or paperwork so that number sits on the piece. Find it further down the Tools list.
Scan Papers photographs receipts, certificates, or appraisal documents and attaches them to a piece, so the paperwork is not in a different drawer. Find it further down the Tools list.
How Complex Is It rates movement complexity from the complications you mark, so a service quote has something to point at. Find it further down the Tools list.
Is It Accurate logs time checks against a reference and tracks daily rate over weeks, so you can see if a watch is gaining or losing. Find it further down the Tools list.
What to Wear — Rotation Planner — assigns pieces for the week so nothing sits unworn too long. Find it further down the Tools list.
Warranties stores expiry dates — HHH reminds you before they lapse, so a claim window does not close unused. Find it further down the Tools list.
Tap Exact Time. HHH shows reference time — use it to set your watch or check the rate.
Tap Moon Phase. See tonight's moon and set a moonphase dial so the complication matches the sky.
On Print and Export List, tap My Museum, Wish list, or For sale, then set columns and generate a PDF — a list you can hand someone without opening the phone.
Tap the Share Nearby QR to show the piece summary — PIN is above; Bluetooth is optional. Pro. Same idea as handing a card, without handing the watch.

Tap Offline Show Pack under Settings before a flea market or show with no signal, so you still have a pocket reference. Identify with a connection is always the better read — use the pack only offline.
Tap View on Big Screen for a slideshow of your collection on a TV or projector — useful when you are showing the museum, not hunting a piece.
From Tools, open Movement to Parts to go from a movement photo or an identification to the parts that fit.
Questions? Email support@josspatech.com or use in-app feedback.
This user guide is at josspatech.com/videos/hhh/user-guide.

Share your wish list with friends or with clock and watch dealers. Sellers can then browse a list of the pieces their contacts are looking to purchase. Open Wish list under My Museum, or tap Tools, then Demand Rolodex, then Send.

Tap Contact and fill Your contact - name is required; add phone, email, and optional website. That contact information is included automatically with the list of pieces you are looking for, so they know how to reach you.
Check the wishes to share, or tap Share all - up to ten wants. Target prices never leave your phone; friends and dealers only see what you want, plus how to reach you.
Tap Send want list, then show them the four-digit PIN and QR, or tap Send nearby over Bluetooth with the same PIN.
As a dealer or seller, open Tools then Demand Rolodex and tap Receive, so a want list someone sent you lands on your phone.
Choose Paste QR or Nearby Bluetooth, enter the buyer’s four-digit PIN, then tap Accept card.
Browse the Demand Rolodex board — pieces your contacts who shared wish lists want to buy, grouped by make and model. Tap a board group for contacts, specs, and notes — no prices on the card.
Phone or email reaches the buyer. A private one-to-ten rating on that contact stays on your phone only.
